title: 'Coffee Laata Hun, Dimaag Nahi Chal Raha': Kid's Mimicry Of Parents' WFH Call Is Spot-On | Video | Viral News - News18
text: Children learn a lot from their parents at an early age, primarily through observation and imitation. By watching how their parents interact, respond to situations, and navigate daily life, they unconsciously absorb behaviours, attitudes and values that shape their worldview. A recent viral video is a perfect example of this. It shows a child hilariously mimicking his parents’ work-from-home routine, right from saying, “Am I audible?" to declaring, “Production issue dekh raha hu." His spot-on imitation has left the Internet in splits, with many joking that he already looks “ready for corporate." Kid Mimics Father’s Job As Corporate Employee The video shared on Instagram depicts a kid, seemingly 4-5 years old, working on a laptop with headphones on, closely resembling a corporate employee working from a work-from-home setting. In the clip, he says, “Am I audible? Let me share my screen. Production issue dekh raha hun, thoda time lagega, ruk ruk ruk. Hello Amar, I will check, I will check, what is the issue? I will check. Hello Laksh, main coffee leke lata hun, mera dimaag nahi chal raha hai. 10 minutes main, haan." How Did Social Media React? The clip quickly caught the attention of viewers, leaving many corporate employees laughing. Reacting to the post, one Instagram user joked, “When recruiters want freshers with 10 years of experience." Another quipped, “He is ready for corporate." Someone added, “He’s so good at mimicking us IT tribe—Coffee leke aata hun, dimaag nahi chal raha (I’ll grab some coffee, my brain isn’t working)." A user wrote, “I’ll check is the biggest commitment ever." Another person wrote, “Just realised this generation is coming, jo apne mummy papa ko: I will send by EOD kehta sunkar bade ho rahe hai." “Ye sidha manager banega (He will directly become the manager)," one of them penned. A person wrote, “He is ready for corporate, no other AI but your son will replace you, he can take over." This often unconscious learning process plays a crucial role in a child’s development, shaping their social skills, emotional regulation and overall outlook on life.
